# Secrets a workflow references that DELIBERATELY do not exist (SEC-101 / SEC-102).
#
# GitHub expands an undefined secret to the empty string, silently. Most of the
# time that is a defect. Sometimes it is the designed behaviour: several report
# sections detect the empty value and render "DATA UNAVAILABLE" with the missing
# variable named, which is exactly what the Workflow & Backup Integrity Policy
# asks for — never a silent green.
#
# This file is where that distinction gets written down. Every entry needs a
# reason AND a Jira key, enforced by scripts/check-workflow-secret-refs.py.
# An absence nobody is tracking is not a decision.
#
# Format:   SECRET_NAME  # why the absence is safe, and what happens (TICKET)
#
# Secrets that DO exist live in .github/known-secrets.txt, generated verbatim
# from `gh secret list`. Never hand-edit that file to silence this check.

# --- Weekly report, Section 20 "Cost Spotcheck" -----------------------------
# probe() marks the provider unavailable and the shaper renders DATA UNAVAILABLE
# naming the missing variable. Cost reporting is a scaffold; no provider API is
# consumed deeply yet.
VERCEL_API_TOKEN            # cost spotcheck renders DATA UNAVAILABLE naming the var (SEC-102)
SUPABASE_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN   # cost spotcheck renders DATA UNAVAILABLE naming the var (SEC-102)

# --- Weekly report + email-as-prompt: Jira reads ----------------------------
# Guarded by an explicit `[ -z ... ]` test that sets skipped_reason, so the
# section renders DATA UNAVAILABLE with the specific cause rather than a zero.
ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN_READONLY  # explicit -z guard -> DATA UNAVAILABLE with reason (SEC-102)
ATLASSIAN_USER_EMAIL          # explicit -z guard -> DATA UNAVAILABLE with reason (SEC-102)
ATLASSIAN_DOMAIN              # explicit -z guard -> DATA UNAVAILABLE with reason (SEC-102)

# --- Authed E2E: Cloudflare WAF bypass --------------------------------------
# NOT benign — a real open blocker, listed here so it stays visible rather than
# failing every PR. Cloudflare bot protection 403s the GitHub runner IP
# (CLAUDE.md gotcha #7), so the authed E2E journey cannot run from CI at all
# until the founder adds a CF WAF skip rule and provisions this header/secret
# pair. Until then that coverage is UNVERIFIED, not passing.

# --- CTL-049 migration ledger parity: Supabase Management API ---------------
# NOT benign, and deliberately NOT silenced — a founder action, tracked.
#
# CTL-049 asks whether supabase/migrations/ can rebuild the databases. Reading
# each project's applied-migration ledger needs a Supabase personal access
# token (GET /v1/projects/{ref}/database/migrations). `scripts/gen-db-types.sh`
# already expects the same variable, but only ever ran on a developer machine,
# so the token has never been provisioned as a repo secret.
#
# Until it is, the `ledger-parity` job in db-invariants.yml fails LOUDLY every
# day with "SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN is not set". That is the intended behaviour
# and matches how the same file already treats an unapplied invariants
# migration: an unrunnable backstop is not a healthy backstop, and it must not
# look like one. The alternative — skipping when the secret is absent — is the
# `if: env.X != ''` pattern KAN-167 forbids and SEC-136 documents live.
#
# ⚠️ This is a NAG, not an expected red. The distinction is that it is tracked,
# actionable, and owned: create the token at
# https://supabase.com/dashboard/account/tokens, add it as the repo secret
# SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, and refresh .github/known-secrets.txt. If it is still
# failing weeks from now, that has become a red people have learned to expect,
# which CLAUDE.md correctly calls a control you have switched off — at that
# point disable the job explicitly and say so, rather than leaving it red.
#
# The comparison logic is NOT blocked on this: `--self-test` runs on every PR
# via pr-checks.yml and exercises the normaliser, the two-way ratchet and the
# fail-closed paths without credentials.
SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN       # CTL-049 fails loudly until the founder provisions it; self-test half runs on every PR (SEC-137)

# --- SEC-143 admin schema-contract check: cross-repo read -------------------
# NOT benign, and it is why that step has never once succeeded — see SEC-150.
#
# db-invariants.yml reads lyra-admin-mcp-server's committed schema contract to
# prove it still matches production (the BUGS-101 defect: the admin server wrote
# against dropped columns for 47 days with nothing watching). The step was built
# using the workflow's built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, citing CTL-043 as precedent.
#
# CTL-043 works because ITS target is PUBLIC — shared-code-manifest.json records
# that precondition beside the repo it names. lyra-admin-mcp-server is PRIVATE,
# and a workflow's built-in token is scoped to its own repository, so it can
# never read that repo. The mechanism was copied without the condition that made
# it valid, and the step went red the day it reached main.
#
# The workflow now reads ADMIN_CONTRACT_READ_TOKEN when present and falls back
# to GITHUB_TOKEN when not — so the absence changes nothing today, and the step
# keeps failing CLOSED with a message naming the real cause. It starts working
# the moment the secret exists, with no further code change.
#
# ⚠️ NAG, not an expected red — same distinction SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN draws
# above. Provision a FINE-GRAINED token with Contents:read on
# luisa-sys/lyra-admin-mcp-server ONLY (no write, no other repo), add it as
# ADMIN_CONTRACT_READ_TOKEN, and refresh .github/known-secrets.txt. A classic
# broad-scope PAT here would be a real downgrade and must not be used. If this
# is still absent weeks from now, the honest move is to disable the step and say
# so, not to leave a permanent red teaching people to scroll past the job.
ADMIN_CONTRACT_READ_TOKEN   # SEC-143 step fails closed naming the cause until provisioned (SEC-150)

# --- Required-checks drift (SEC-106 / CTL-066) ------------------------------
# Reading branch protection needs `administration:read`, which GITHUB_TOKEN does
# not carry at any `permissions:` setting — it is a repository-administration
# scope available only to a fine-grained PAT or a GitHub App installation token.
# required-checks.yml falls back to GITHUB_TOKEN on purpose, so the step RUNS and
# reports UNVERIFIED (exit 2) naming the missing permission, rather than being
# skipped. Skipping on a missing secret is the `if: env.X != ''` silent-skip the
# Workflow Integrity Policy forbids outright, and is how health-check.yml sat
# dark for a month while reporting green (SEC-79).
#
# ⚠️ NAG, not an expected red — same distinction ADMIN_CONTRACT_READ_TOKEN draws
# above. Provision a FINE-GRAINED PAT on luisa-sys/lyra ONLY, with
# Administration: Read-only and nothing else (no write, no other repo), add it as
# BRANCH_PROTECTION_READ_TOKEN, and refresh .github/known-secrets.txt. The
# control starts measuring with no further code change. Until then the `--live`
# arm proves nothing — and note the `--local` arm in pr-checks.yml needs no
# credentials and is unaffected, so a job rename is still caught today.
BRANCH_PROTECTION_READ_TOKEN  # SEC-106 --live reports UNVERIFIED naming the missing scope until provisioned (SEC-106)
